strings.name: Allyson Felix
strings.summary: Felix began track at a Los Angeles high school and continued university studies after turning professional. She won world and Olympic titles in the 200m, 400m and relays, reaching eleven Olympic medals by the Tokyo Games. After becoming a mother, she spoke publicly about maternity protection in sponsorship and maternal health. She ended that phase of competition in 2022 and announced preparations for a Los Angeles Olympic comeback in 2026; qualification remains a goal.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones verifiable through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A champion at multiple Olympics, she also advances maternity protection for women athletes.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied elementary education at the University of Southern California; attended Los Angeles Baptist High School.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Sprint and relay achievements
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won eleven medals, including seven golds, across five Olympics in individual sprints and team relays.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Maternity protection advocacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Publicly addressed sponsorship treatment during pregnancy and childbirth and advocates for maternal health.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Announces comeback preparations
strings.timeline.t1.text: Said she planned to return to competition and seek a place at Los Angeles 2028; this remains an unfulfilled goal.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Ends previous competitive chapter
strings.timeline.t2.text: Ended that phase of professional competition after the Oregon World Championships, continuing business and charitable work.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Olympic medals reach eleven
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won 400m bronze and 4×400m gold in Tokyo, taking her Olympic total to eleven.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Speaks on maternity protection
strings.timeline.t4.text: After becoming a mother, criticized sponsorship treatment during pregnancy and childbirth, advancing athlete-rights debate.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Three London golds
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the 200m, 4×100m and 4×400m, taking gold in individual and team events.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First world title
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the women’s 200m in Helsinki, beginning three consecutive world titles in the event.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Athens Olympic silver
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won 200m silver at her first Olympics, joining the leading international competitors.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Turns professional after school
strings.timeline.t8.text: Signed as a professional after high school while continuing university education.
